items.title: Bobby Watson interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, January 19, 1996
items.q: So when I got a chance to study with him, that’s one of the reasons I went to the University of Miami, was to study with Clifton Williams.

ctx.x: Tell us about you know, some of the things you’re saying are fabulous because they’re insights of personal experience that you have as to the sound. But you’ve also studied composition and theory haven’t you? Tell us about your time of study.

Oh, I studied with a man, his name was Clifton Williams. And he is very big in the concert band field. He has several things published. We played them when I was in high school. So when I got a chance to study with him, that’s one of the reasons I went to the University of Miami, was to study with Clifton Williams. And he taught me as a composer, not as a jazz composer. He said, “I want you to be a good composer, so that way, whatever you want to do, whether it be jazz or classical, you will at least have the…

to give pride. Or boredom is like [scats]. Like that you know? And so you’d have to guess, and depending on the value of the notes and how hard you hit the notes, you find that those are your tools in composition. That you manipulate the notes and then by doing that you manipulate people’s emotions. And it’s a very exciting thing. So that’s how I write now. Sometimes the chords come first, but most of the time I go for the melody. And I keep a little journal if I hear something I’ll write it down and then I’ll…
